100	- F-237 **The well-formedness walk reports an ill-formed type whose span lies outside the expression that the walk is in at that expression, so a call whose static argument breaks the bound of the callee's result type is reported at the call.** A call's type keeps the spans of the callee's declared type. An error on such a type is reported at the innermost expression the walk met it in, once for each call that made the type: the expressions that a call's value flows to share its type node and add no error, and a second call with the same printed static argument gets its own error. One known gap, still open (row 776): of two nested calls of one callee at static arguments that print alike, `next[\T\](next[\T\](x))`, only the inner call is reported; the program is still refused. Where the type is ill-formed where it is written, its error stays at the declaration. A local variable's right-hand side is walked before the lines that use the variable, so a call whose value a variable holds is reported at the call, not at a later use. In the library, by reading, reporting at the call adds and drops no error against reporting at the declaration, and the distance holds no well-formedness error (F-53). Source: `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/TypeWellFormedChecker.scala`, `check`, `error`, `outside` and `within`, and its `SLocalVarDecl` case. Gated by `compiler_tests/XXXStaticArgBoundAtCall`, `XXXStaticArgBoundAtCallOnce`, `XXXStaticArgBoundAtEachCall`, `XXXStaticArgBoundAtCallNotAtUse` and `XXXIllFormedTypeAtDeclarationOnce`, and `XXXStaticArgBoundNestedCall`, which pins row 776's single error. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-checker-abstract-callsite/REPORT.md` sections 1 and 6, its `SKEPTIC.md` sections 5.1 and 5.2 and its `JUDGE.md`.
101	- F-240 **The checker's count stage takes about 150 s and its distance stage 227 s at the last landed gate, climb batch 22's.** At climb batch 15b's gate they took 325 s and 1,075 s; the solver's memos (F-235) make most of the difference, not load. Load can lengthen a stage more than twofold: climb batch 16's merged code took 217 s for the distance stage at its gate, at a load average of 3.3, and nearly the same code took 574 s at 4.6 to 5.3. So a time compares only with one taken under a like load. Source: the gate's call times and `compile-ladder/climb-batch-22/gate/distance.txt`. Detail: `reviews/batch-22-review.md`, section 2; `reviews/batch-21b-review.md`, section 2; `reviews/batch-17-review.md`, section 1; `reviews/batch-16-review.md`, section 2.
102	- F-242 **`SUM`'s fusion pairs with `MAX` and `MIN` hold no site of the distance: a `where` condition on each of `SumReduction`'s two `distribute` overloads clears their four unmet bounds, and `ActualReduction`'s generic `distribute`, which `SumReduction` inherits, with its result over its own `K`, clears their two return-type errors.** The fusion pairs are `MaxSumReductionPair`, `MinSumReductionPair` and those two overloads, through which the team's `Generator2` computes the maximum or the minimum of sums in one pass. The two errors were at the two overloads, which answer a pair over `Maybe[\T\]` beside the inherited `distribute`. With the inherited one answering `PossibleReductionPair[\K\]`, they pass the return-type rule (F-75). The team's commented text, which answers `PossibleReductionPair[\R\]`, only moves the two errors to the generic. The fusion stays (P-151). Row 433, fixed; F-250 gives the landing and its test. Detail: `perf-probes/where-clauses/REPORT.md` A.1 and A.2.1; `perf-probes/generic-distribute/REPORT.md` sections 3 and 4.
103	- F-243 **The 13 errors that were filed as waiting on `where` clauses, 13 of the distance's 49 at the gates of climb batches 15b and 16, are all cleared; the 13th, the list comparisons' site, by conditional extension.** The where-clauses probe traced each of them (A.1). The method condition and the generic `distribute` clear the fusion pairs' 6 (F-242). `AnyList`'s `comprises { List[\E\] } where [\E\]` clause, a comment of the team's made live, clears its 4, with its bodies respelled within `AnyList` and none moved into `List` (F-251). A `cast` at `additiveIdentity`'s and `multiplicativeIdentity`'s fallbacks, `else => 0` and `else => 1`, clears 2 (row 436). Conditional extension cleared the list comparisons' site (the list half of row 634; its tuple half was built earlier), with `ZeroIndexed[\E\]` and an element-wise `=` kept outside the condition (F-255). By the probe, library edits with no new language would also have cleared 12: dropping the fusion pairs, moving `AnyList`'s bodies into `List`, and the `cast` at the fallbacks. Detail: `perf-probes/where-clauses/REPORT.md` A.0, A.1, A.4, B.0 and B.3; `reviews/batch-17-review.md`, section 2.
104	- F-244 **The three `where` forms that the checker builds (P-151: conditional extension, a function's or a method's condition, and `AnyList`'s `comprises` clause) hold where the where-clauses probe tested them; of the probe's two holes, one stands: a member checked under a conditional extension's condition stays callable where the condition fails (row 773; F-255).** A type variable opened from a `comprises` clause passes the probe's escape, two-value and Amin–Tate tests: the opened type is refused where another type is declared, two values get two types, and Amin and Tate's unsound shape is refused (F-251). The other hole is closed: a method's constraint on its trait's parameter bounds that parameter inside the method and is checked at a dotted call (row 748; F-256). Swift, Rust and Haskell scope such a member to the condition (B.3), which P-151 holds as still to build. The opening of a `comprises` clause has two other open rows of the gap ledger in the checker, 751 and 752; a third, row 775, a crash on such a trait's override, is fixed (F-281). F-250 (row 470) and F-256 give the constraints that the checker does not yet read. Detail: `perf-probes/where-clauses/REPORT.md` B.1 to B.3 and B.6.
105	- F-245 **With every symbolic operator checked for overloading, the compiled checker finds 5 errors in the library on climb batch 21's first run's code, the distance's 5, where that batch's base gave 191.** The checker checks every operator (F-281), so the distance stage is this check; it gave these 5 with no crash, and gives 0 since climb batch 22 cleared them (F-53). The 191 were measured by the full-check stage, a copy of the checker with every operator admitted that caught crashes per name (`perf-probes/symbolic-operators-2/run-shadow.sh`), whose edits no longer match the tree; on climb batch 21's first run's code it caught the `AnyList` crash on `||` (row 809, fixed). Of the base's 186 errors beyond the 5, the library's known fixes clear 54 (F-276), the index bound 124 (F-278, P-156) and the exclusion test 8 (F-277, P-157); measured together on the merged tree, nothing comes. Walk's meet check skips symbolic operators (row 611); widened the same way at `d212b2c1f`, it refused only `EmptyString`'s `||` (F-142). Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-symbolic-check/REPORT.md` section 5; `compile-ladder/climb-batch-21/RECORD.md`, "The tests on the merged tree"; `reviews/batch-21-review.md`, section 1; `perf-probes/symbolic-operators-2/REPORT.md` sections 0 to 2; `perf-probes/symbolic-operators/REPORT.md` section 1.5.
106	- F-250 **Inside a declaration, the compiled checker reads a `where` clause's trait constraint `X extends B` as a bound of `X`, and it adds a constraint on the declaration's own static parameter to that parameter's bound in the declaration's arrow (its function type), so a call is checked against it.** So a method's condition on its trait's or object's static parameter bounds that parameter in the method's body (`compiler_tests/WhereBoundMethodChecker`), and a call that breaks a function's own constraint is refused (`compiler_tests/XXXWhereBoundFunctionCall`, which refuses `g("s")`). The count, and walk's element types, did not change. Detail: `explorations/compile-ladder/rung-anylist-comprises/REPORT.md`.
108	- F-254 **In the compiled checker, a function or method that leaves out its return type takes it from the one declaration of the exported api whose parameter types are the function's own.** `ApiTypeExtractor` compares the parameter types as the export check does (`ExportChecker.equalTypes`), and a parameter that the function leaves untyped matches any type. It takes the return type only if exactly one api declaration of the name matches. With none or several, it takes none, and the declaration is left as written. So the choice does not depend on the JVM's identity-hash order of the declarations, and no output of the count or distance stage is known to move with that order (F-232): the error at `Library/FortressLibrary.fss:130` (`BIG LEXICO`'s omitted return type), which came and went with that order, is gone from both stages. Evidence: read in `scala_src/typechecker/ApiTypeExtractor.scala:77-126` and `:193-209`. Tests: `compiler_tests/OmittedReturnTypeFromApi`, `OmittedMethodReturnTypeFromApi`. Detail: `explorations/compile-ladder/rung-checker-four-rows/REPORT.md`, sections 1 and 5.
109	- F-255 **The compiled checker reads conditional extension in its subtype relation: a trait or object that extends a type under a `where` clause that binds no variable and holds trait constraints only is a subtype of that type exactly where the constraints hold.** The `extends` entry itself, an object's value parameters and every member are checked with the constraints holding. The static parameters, the declaration's own `where` clause, its `excludes` and `comprises` clauses and its other `extends` entries are checked without them. The disambiguator drops every trait's and object's `throws` clause and contract, so these are not checked at all (row 781). A clause that binds a variable, or that holds a constraint that is not a trait constraint, is read as before: as a parent at every instance. Limits: a member checked under the condition stays callable where the condition fails (row 773), and walk and the compiled run time read the extension at every instance (row 774). Other readers of the `extends` clause in the checker ignore the condition. Those that go through the type's parents see a conditional parent at no instance: the ancestors (`TypeAnalyzer.ancestors`), which the overloading checker reads to let a concrete method implement an abstract one. Those that read the clause itself see it at every instance: the inherited `excludes` clauses (`TypeAnalyzer.excludesClause`). None of these readers moved a result on the library, and no ledger row holds them (report section 10). In the library, `List` extends `LexicographicOrder[\List[\E\],E\]` only where `E extends StandardTotalOrder[\E\]`; its `ZeroIndexed[\E\]` entry and its own element-wise `opr =` stand outside the condition, so every list keeps them (`Library/List.fss:106-107`, `:124-128`). On the rung's own tree, against climb batch 17's gate, this cleared the site `FortressLibrary.fss:2063` and added none. Tests: `compiler_tests/CondExtendChecker`, `XXXCondExtendRefuseChecker`, `XXXCondExtendUnconditionalEntryChecker`, `XXXCondExtendExcludesChecker`, `XXXCondExtendComprisesChecker`, `XXXCondExtendParamBoundChecker`, `XXXCondExtendExcludesWhereChecker`, `CondExtendInheritedMember` (a type that inherits through a conditional parent compiles: the code generator's analyzer reads the parent at every instance), `tests/XXXConditionalExtensionTypeTestWalk`. Detail: `explorations/compile-ladder/rung-checker-conditional-extension/REPORT.md`, sections 1, 6 and 10.
110	- F-256 **The compiled checker checks a `where` clause's trait constraints where they apply.** At a dotted call, a candidate whose `where` clause constrains its trait's or object's static parameter is not applicable where the receiver's static argument breaks the constraint ('Method Holder[\String\].showIt is not applicable: its where clause requires String to extend Shows.'). If a function's or method's `where` clause has a trait constraint, the clause's `nat` and `int` variables become static parameters of its arrow, inferred at the call. So a constraint whose bound names such a variable is met where some value of it meets every constraint. When the type variables' solutions leave only size constraints, the solver tries once more to solve them. Walk and the compiled path both refuse a function's or method's type `where`-clause variable at name binding ('E is undefined.'), so this inference never reaches one. A trait's or object's own constraint is checked where its type is used, with the bound's message, also at a constructor call through the call's type. A type `where`-clause variable of a `comprises` clause is bounded by its binding and by the clause's constraints on it, where it is opened and in the check of an extender. In a bound that names the variable itself, as `E extends StandardTotalOrder[\E\]` does, the opened type stands for the variable. Not read: at a dotted call, a constraint on the trait's or object's static parameter whose bound names the method's own static parameters or `where`-clause variables; at a type's use, a constraint whose bound names a `where`-clause variable; and a static argument written at a top-level call (row 470). Walk still runs a dotted call that breaks a method's condition (row 777), and a `comprises` clause's `where`-clause variable captures a same-named static parameter in another declaration's bound (row 778). These checks moved no site of the count or the distance (F-53 holds the current values). Tests: `compiler_tests/XXXWhereBoundDottedCallChecker`, `WhereVariableBoundCallChecker`, `XXXWhereConstraintTypeUseChecker`, `XXXWhereConstraintExtendsChecker`, `XXXComprisesWhereBoundExtenderChecker`, `OpenTypeWhereConstraintChecker`, `XXXComprisesWhereConstraintExtenderChecker`, `OpenTypeWhereSelfBoundChecker`. Detail: `explorations/compile-ladder/rung-checker-where-checks/REPORT.md`, sections 1 and 6, and `SKEPTIC.md` beside it.

- F-66 **The checker-count stage's table, `gate/checker-count.txt`, lands with every batch beside the gate's `summary.txt`.** Its total at the last landed gate is F-53's count. Step 8 of a batch's gate compares it with the newest landed table. The total is never red on its own, as P-39 rules, since a fix can raise it and the effects of two rungs on it do not add up. The gate is red on a crash line that no rung declared in its manifest (`expectedCheckerCrash`), on a table with no total, and on a stale shadow: the instrumented copy of `StaticChecker` beside the stage (`checker-count/shadow-src/`), when the tracked `StaticChecker` no longer matches the checksum that `run.sh` records. Detail: `coordinator/climb-batch-workflow.md`, "The checker count, and a rung whose test is that stage".
- F-67 **The compiled type checker checks `nat` and `int` static parameters.** A size is a size parameter's name, a literal or an operation on sizes. Two sizes are equal when their written forms are, once each operation on numerals is computed, so `2 3` equals `6` but `m n` does not equal `n m` (F-146). The checker refuses to infer a `bool`, `dim` or `unit` static argument (`XXXNatBoolChecker`). It does not compare `bool` arguments, so `object F extends { Flag[\true\], Flag[\false\] }`, two instantiations of one trait, passes it, and code generation then stops on it (row 406, open, a part of P-40 still to build). A call that leaves a size unknown is refused, "Could not infer static argument ... without context"; F-69 gives when an overload set is refused and when it is not. It builds P-40. Gated by `compiler_tests/NatInferredChecker`, `NatWrittenChecker`, `NatMethodChecker`, `NatExportChecker` and `XXXNatMismatchChecker`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-nat-checker/REPORT.md` section 1.
- F-68 **The checker's return-type rule reads a size as it reads a type parameter.** A size of the less specific declaration that the domains leave unsolved stays that declaration's own parameter, as `Papers/Types/overloading-check.tick` binds `Δ2`. So an override returning `Dn[\T,3,s\]` over `Up[\T,b,s\]` is refused, like its type-parameter twin, and the library's `subarray` override passes. Gated by `compiler_tests/NatOverrideChecker` and `XXXNatRetSizeChecker`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-nat-checker/REPORT.md` section 5.
- F-69 **The compiled checker refuses a call whose most specific arm failed only on a size that the call cannot fix, when that arm's parameter types are free of the size.** The message is "Could not infer static argument nat n without context". It drops instead an arm whose unknown size is in its own parameter types (row 400, open). It lets through a call whose argument's static type lies above the arm's domain, and the compiled run dies reading the size (row 446, open). It builds P-40. Gated by `compiler_tests/NatKnownSizeArm`, which compiles and runs a call that fixes the size, and `XXXNatUnknownSize*`, which pin the refusal's message; rows 400 and 446 have no test. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-unknown-size-arm/REPORT.md` section 10.
- F-70 **The compiled checker checks a static argument written at a dotted method call against its parameter's bound, but not one written at a top-level function call.** At a dotted call it puts the written arguments into each bound and refuses a call whose argument misses one, "No such method" (row 651, fixed). At a top-level call it matches kinds only, so `n[\String\]("d")` passes for `n[\T extends Number\](s: String): T` (row 470, open). Gated by `compiler_tests/MethodStaticArgsBoundNamesOther*`, which accept a dotted call whose written arguments meet their bounds. No test pins the refusal of an argument that misses its bound; a probe showed it (`rung-checker-contexts/REPORT.md` section 6). Row 470 can have no gated test, since the harness has no form for a program that the specification refuses and the checker accepts. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-checker-contexts/REPORT.md` section 1.
- F-71 **The compiled checker does not narrow the variable of the shorthand form `typecase x of T => ...`, neither path accepts the binding form `typecase x = e of`, and the clause-binding form `typecase e of y: T => ... end` runs on both paths.** So write the clause-binding form, as the library does (F-134): its `cast` writes `typecase x of x':T => x' ... end`. In the shorthand form, the checker refuses a clause that uses `x` as a `T`, and such a clause runs under walk only; a clause that does not, as in the library's `instanceOf`, passes. The binding form parses as the equality `x = e`. Only the specification's grammar has it, under the team's note that the section awaits the pattern-matching proposal (`typecase.tex:15`). Row 460 records both refusals, and no test gates them. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-exclusion-remainder/REPORT.md` section 15.
- F-72 **The compiled checker reads a `comprises` clause for a generic subtrait as the team's 2012 texts do (Luchangco's Types chapter and Welterweight; P-44): the subtrait may extend the closed trait when the trait table knows at least one type that immediately extends the subtrait, and each such type is below a listed type.** It builds P-44. This rule leaves the ellipsis refusal of F-64 (row 354, open) as it was. Open: an extender in another compilation unit escapes the check, the hole that P-44 leaves (row 487). The verdict changes when the extender renames its type variable (row 489), and the extenders are found by the simple text of the trait's name (row 490). Gated by `compiler_tests/ComprisesGenericSubtrait`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-comprises-checker/REPORT.md` section 6.
- F-73 **The compiled checker infers a generic's static arguments with coercion: a type parameter that is the whole type of each parameter it occurs in, as `T` in `pick[\T\](x: T, y: T)`, takes the narrowest type that every one of its arguments converts into and its bound permits.** It looks for that type among its arguments' types, their coercion targets and its bound, the bound only when it is a trait type other than `Object` or `Any`. It builds P-74 and P-49. A coerced declaration ranks below one that needs no coercion. A tie among coerced declarations is refused, "Ambiguous coercion", outside three narrow cases (the report's section 3.2). When the tied declarations differ only at positions where the call passes a numeral, the checker reads the numeral as `ZZ32`, or as `ZZ64` or `ZZ` when its value does not fit; that reading is a default. The coercion attempt refuses a call beyond 64 combinations of candidate types (row 506) and a call with an untyped function argument (row 507). Gated by `compiler_tests/NatLitArgChecker`, `CoercionGenericFnCompiledRungC` and `InferCoercionShapes`, which F-51 also cites, and the refusal of a tie by `XXXInferAmbiguousCoercion`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-inference-checker/REPORT.md` section 3.2.
- F-74 **Under walk, an integer numeral takes its type from its value: a `ZZ32` if it fits 32 bits, a `ZZ64` if it fits 64 bits, a `ZZ` above that; it stays so until walk has the checker's static types, since without them a list of numerals and a generic's static argument take their types from the values.** Its run-time type is the library's value object `Int`, `Long` or `BigNum`, below `ZZ32`, `ZZ64` and `ZZ` (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fsi:125`, `:128`, `:223`). Walk instantiates a generic at it, so a `Box[\Int\]` is a type apart from `Box[\ZZ32\]` and dispatches past it (row 364). F-74 is why P-76's walk half waits; F-79 is the library half, built. Probe Q (`compile-ladder/plan-n/probe-q/PROBE-Q.md`) measured walk with every integer numeral an `IntLiteral`, the numeral's own type in the library. It ran before climb batch N's second run and before the library half landed. Alone, the switch changed 59 test verdicts. With four devices (a numeral at an `AnyIntegral` parameter read as `ZZ32`, `ZZ64` or `ZZ`, a tuple of numerals converted at dispatch, `asif` converting, a varargs list converted at dispatch), the library loaded and both microGPT checks kept their values, but 24 passing interpreter tests failed: 6 by design, 3 of them team tests that assert a `ZZ32`; 9 for want of static types (rows 364, 510); and 9 walk gaps. A size used as a value is a `ZZ32` up to 2^31-1 and a `ZZ64` above (row 486; F-140). Detail: `reviews/numeral-switch-judgement.md` sections 2 and 3.
- F-75 **The compiled checker checks the Return Type Rule over every instance, and a positional rule: when two generic declarations in the more-specific relation declare as many static parameters of their own, those parameters agree in kind by position, and the more specific return type is a subtype of the other once the other's parameters are read as its own by position.** The equal-count scope and the comparison of kinds are the rung's choices. It builds P-45. Checking every instance, as P-45 asks, it also refuses a generic declaration beside a plain one whose domain is an object type, a pair that the type group's 2011 paper (`Papers/Types/`) accepts, since the paper sets aside the instances whose domains cannot meet (row 542, open). In the interpreter's library the two rules refuse no pair: the distance holds no return-type or overloading error (F-53). Gated by `compiler_tests/OverloadGeneric*` and `OverloadBoundNamesForced`, which accept; `XXXOverloadReturnEveryInstance` and `XXXOverloadPermutedStaticParams`, which pin the two rules' refusals; and `XXXOverloadReturnObjectDomain`, which pins row 542's. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-return-type-rule/decision-record.md` sections 1 and 2.
- F-76 **The compiled checker accepts the specification's `comprises` example of the Meet Rule (`Specification/advanced/overloading.tex`, "The Meet Rule for Functions") by a coverage check used only in overload checking, not in its subtype test, and types a call whose argument's static type lies below closed traits and above the types that they list by the intersection of the return types of its most specific declarations, when they tie without coercion.** It builds P-60, which reads `comprises` at the level of values: several declarations below two overloads serve as their meet if together they cover it. Open: coverage refuses a pair when a declaration that it compares has static parameters (row 546). In an accepted family that has any other generic declaration, such a call is typed by the head of a sort, which follows declaration order and can vary between runs, not by the intersection (row 543). That narrower scope than P-60's is a default. On the compiled path, a method call on a value typed by the intersection crashes the code generator (row 540), and a generic declaration instantiated at an intersection type dies as it loads (row 559). The checker checks a `comprises` clause only at the closed trait's immediate subtypes, so a type in another component below a generic subtrait escapes it (row 487). Its verdict on an overload set can depend on the components compiled before it in the same JVM (row 547). Gated by `compiler_tests/*Comprises*` and `*CoverageReturn*`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-return-type-rule/decision-record.md` sections 3 and 4.
- F-77 **The one library repairs its refused overload families with its own exclusions, and the checker accepts its `seq` pairs by the rule for functional methods (F-80).** It builds P-45. `StandardMin`, `StandardMax`, `SequentialGenerator` and `FilterGenerator` exclude `HasRank`, `String` excludes `AnyMultiplicativeRing`, and `TotalComparison` extends `StandardMinMax` (P-98). Marker traits instead would give two ordered types several minimal common supertypes, which walk mishandles (rows 555, 589). Gated by `tests/LibraryOverloadFamilies.fss`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-overload-families/REPORT.md` section 4.
- F-78 **The compiled checker instantiates a type parameter that nothing at a call fixes at the intersection of its upper bounds, never `BottomType`, and tries a call by subtyping without the expected type first.** It builds P-48 and P-49. Where the call has an expected type, its attempts come in this order: subtyping without the expected type, kept when its result converts to it; subtyping with the expected type; coercion with it; and coercion without it. The second lets a call whose untyped function argument only the expected type fixes type-check, since the coercion attempt cannot check such an argument (row 507). P-49 decides the first and the third; the second and the fourth are an agent's choice, the instance-bound rung's (its decision record, D4). An argument of intersection type fixes a parameter at the whole intersection, not at one conjunct (row 541). The run time has no class for an intersection type, so such an instance dies as it loads (row 559). Gated by `compiler_tests/InferResultOnly*` and `InferContextKeepsFit`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-instance-bound/REPORT.md` sections 1 and 7; the order, by reading, `compile-ladder/rung-instance-bound/decision-record.md`, D4, and `scala_src/typechecker/impls/Functionals.scala:733-737`.
- F-79 **In the interpreter's library, `IntLiteral`, the type that the compiled checker gives an integer numeral, is declared on the model of the compiler's prelude: a sibling of the number types under `Number`, which each integer type, `QQ`, `RR64` and `AnyIntegral` convert from by coercion.** It builds the library half of P-76. Under walk a numeral is still a `ZZ32`, `ZZ64` or `ZZ`, so no numeral reaches these declarations until walk's half is built (F-74). `IntLiteral` declares itself the members of `Integral[\I\]` that a numeral could not reach, among them the getters `zero` and `one`, `odd`, `even`, `floor` and `DIVIDES`. There are three reasons: for some, no declaration of `Integral` applies to a sibling type even with coercion; for others, the declarations that apply by coercion tie; and a getter must be the type's own member. Each integer type declares its own comparisons, `CMP`, `MAXNUM` and `MINNUM`, and a `^` with an `IntLiteral` exponent. Without them, a typed integer with a numeral operand ties between a declaration inherited from a generic trait and the same operator's own declarations in `ZZ64`, `QQ` and `RR64`. The compiled checker refuses `(3).minimum` and `(3).maximum`, `ZZ32`'s getters (row 581). Gated under walk by `tests/IntegerOrderNumerals.fss`, which checks each integer type's own comparisons, `MAXNUM` and `MINNUM`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-numeral-library/REPORT.md` sections 4 and 6.
- F-80 **The compiled checker judges two functional methods of one name, abstract declarations included, by the Meet Rule for Functional Methods in each type that provides both.** Such a type must provide their meet, compared without the `self` parameter. F-88 says what a type provides. An abstract functional method beside a concrete one in the same trait, with the same parameter types, is refused by the No Duplicates Rule. Unchecked: a pair that only an object expression provides (row 570). It checks every operator, a symbol such as `+`, `<`, `||` or a subscript as well as a name of capitals such as `CAP` or a word such as `juxtaposition` (F-281). The checker's overloading memo is keyed on all the inputs of the check, so a pair accepted at the top level is not reused unchecked in a trait that provides it. Gated by `compiler_tests/FunctionalMethodMeet*`, and by the refusals that the specification asks for, `XXXFunctionalMethodMeetAbstractSibling`, `XXXNoDuplicatesRuleAbstract` and, for an operator, `XXXFunctionalMethodMeetOperatorChecker`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-overloading-checker/REPORT.md` sections 5 and 7; `compile-ladder/rung-checker-abstract-callsite/REPORT.md` section 1.
- F-81 **In the interpreter's library, every Meet Rule pair inside one type that the compiled checker checks has a declaration on its meet, and the checker checks every operator (F-281).** `String`'s juxtaposition is three top-level operators, since two functional methods with `self` at different positions have no meet. `String`'s `||`, `|||`, `//` and `///`, which paired `(a:Any, self)` with `(self, b:Any)`, the shape the specification refuses, are now three top-level operators each too (F-276). F-245's measurement found other invalid pairs, among them `Indexed`'s three subscripts in 17 types, valid since the index bound (F-278). The rung that added these meets also set the declared types listed in report section 1 to what their bodies answer. `__bigOperator2`'s fused branch, whose arm's type the `typecase` cannot show, casts its result to the declared `O0` (F-85). Gated by `tests/LibraryMeetDeclarations.fss`, and for the symbolic operators by the distance stage, which finds no overloading error in the library (F-245). Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-library-meets/REPORT.md` section 1.
- F-82 **In the interpreter's library, the range types declare a method on the meet for each of their Meet Rule pairs that the compiled checker checks, and their declared types match what their bodies answer.** Among the meets are `CAP` at each rank, a range's number of dimensions (F-89 holds the ranks' kinds), and `FullRange`'s abstract `IN`, so a numeral `IN` a `#` or `:` range type-checks (row 580, fixed). The pairs of `Indexed`'s three subscripts have no meet in the ranges and need none since the index bound (F-278). Open library bug (row 603): the full sequential ranges' `map` answers a `SimpleMappedSeqIndexed`, which is no `MappedGenerator`, so its `reverse` is `Indexed`'s. The elements and their order are right, but the string differs: `seq(0:6:2).map(fn x => x + 1).reverse.asString` prints `SimpleReversedIndexed(mapped(seq(1,3,5,7)))`, not `mapped(7,5,3,1)`. `tests/RangeDeclarations.fss` pins that string, and gates the meets. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-range-meets/REPORT.md` section 1.
- F-83 **In the interpreter's library, the string components `String.fss` and `FlatString.fss` hold no site of the distance, the compiled checker's errors in that library (F-53), and the rung's repairs of their refused declarations are in forms that the library already uses.** The trait `String` is declared in `FortressLibrary`, not in `String.fss`, which holds string objects and traits such as `CatString` and `SubString`. `String`'s api writes `abstract` on the members its component's trait leaves without a body or does not declare, and its `excludes` clause is the component's (F-286), so `String` has no entry in the `FortressLibrary` export error. `FlatString`'s api declares its component's header, `extends { String, DelegatedIndexed[\Char, ZZ32\] }`, and no `opr ||(a:FlatString, self)` (F-259). Open library bugs: `FlatString.rangeContains` finds only the first occurrence of the character, and so does `CatString`'s, through its flat halves (row 607). An implicit strided subscript `[:b:c]` is completed from the axis's right end, not from its left as `l:b:c`: `"abcdef"[:3:2]` is `bd`, not `ac` (row 609; the expected failure `tests/XXXSubscriptImplicitStridedRange.fss` holds the specification's answer). Gated by `tests/StringPieces.fss`, which pins row 607's two wrong `false` answers. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-string-slips/REPORT.md` sections 4 and 8.
- F-84 **In the interpreter's library, the result-only type parameters of `fail`, `builtinPrimitive` and `List`'s comprehension operator `BIG <|[\T\]|>` are unbounded, as the team declared them, and the same rung repaired 25 of the compiled checker's 60 one-off error sites in numbers, orderings, `List` and natives, each by a declared type, a body or an api header, in forms that the library already uses.** A result-only parameter occurs only in the result type. P-48 gives it the intersection of its upper bounds, narrowed by the expected type, so where `()` is expected its instance is `()`. The rung also made `MatchFailure` an unchecked exception: it extends `UncheckedException` (row 590). The sites that it left have rows (report section 5). Limit: under walk the name `IntLiteral` also denotes a value, a zero that no numeral reaches, and its arithmetic answers a `ZZ32` against its declared `IntLiteral` (row 578). F-263 holds the integer powers' types, and F-255 `List`'s ordering. The compiler's prelude has instead `fail(s: String): Zilch` (`Library/CompilerLibrary.fsi:33`), a declared bottom result that Steele put in place of the generic `fail` in `0886e9654` (2011-06-13), and it does not bind the one library, since the team's later word makes `Bottom` inexpressible in a program (the 2012 Types chapter; POPL 2019, `research/extracts/ParkPOPL2019.txt:437-438`) and binds an unfixed parameter by its bounds and the expected type, P-48's rule; walk cannot evaluate `Zilch`. Gated under walk by `tests/NumberOrderListDeclarations.fss`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-number-order-slips/REPORT.md` sections 1, 4 and 5.
- F-85 **In the interpreter's library, the rung's repairs of the generator, condition, reduction and nested-generator declarations that the compiled checker refused are in forms that the library already uses. `__bigOperator2`'s fused branch passes its result through `cast[\O0\]`.** That branch, the `typecase` branch that runs a nested big operator through `generate2`, casts its result to `O0` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:1476`), the library's device for an arm whose type the `typecase` cannot show (F-264), so the checker no longer types its body `OR(I0,O0)` where `O0` is declared (row 632) and no site of these declarations is on the distance (F-53). Each method body of `Condition` that calls `cond` writes the call's result type as its static argument, such as `cond[\Maybe[\G\]\]`. The sites that the rung left were cleared by other work: F-250 holds the identity functions' `cast` and the typed `embiggen`, F-93 how library code reads a generator's size and index (row 629), and F-144 how the reductions without an identity are typed at their element type (row 628). Gated by `tests/GeneratorDeclarations.fss` and `tests/NestedReductionFusion.fss`, which run the arm fused, and the cast by the distance stage. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-generator-slips/REPORT.md` sections 5 and 8; `compile-ladder/rung-body-arguments/REPORT.md` section 9.
- F-86 **The compiled checker types a varargs parameter as the team's `ImmutableArray[\T, ZZ32\]`, and applies a varargs declaration by the specification's expansion rule.** The rule reads such a declaration as one declaration for each number of arguments that it can take (`Specification/basic/overloading.tex`, "Applicability for Functionals with Varargs and Keyword Parameters"). Over the interpreter's library, a body uses the parameter as that array. The compiled library declares no `ImmutableArray`, so under it each use of such a parameter is refused (row 604). The code generator refuses varargs (row 624). Gated by `compiler_tests/Varargs*`, and the refusals by the `XXXVarargs*` tests of rows 604 and 624. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-checker-defects/REPORT.md` section 4.
- F-87 **Besides the contexts that it already had, such as a typed declaration's right-hand side, the compiled checker gives a call its expected type in a clause of an `if` without `else` (the type `()`), a block's last expression after local declarations, a `typecase` clause, a juxtaposition, an operator repeated between three or more operands, a `label` body and each value that an `exit` gives the `label`, and, by a retry of the enclosing call, another call's argument.** The inference chapter lists every context (`Specification/basic/inference.tex`, "The Static Arguments of a Call", "The expected type"). In a juxtaposition or a repeated operator, the expression's own expected type goes to the application that it makes. The `label` contexts build P-50. At another call's argument, it retries the enclosing call against each declaration's parameter type, as P-51 decides (F-221). F-226 gives how it renames an inherited method's static parameters at a call, and F-70 where it checks a written static argument against its bound. Gated by `compiler_tests/InferResultOnly*`, among them `InferResultOnlyLabelBody`, a type-check test, since the code generator has no `label`, and `Infer*Context`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-checker-contexts/REPORT.md` section 1.
- F-88 **The compiled checker reads what a trait or object provides by the traits chapter's inheritance, and checks an overriding declaration's return type against the one it overrides.** A type provides its own methods and its immediate supertypes', less those that an own declaration overrides or repeats in its parameter types. So an object below a trait that redeclares an inherited method abstract must define it. The code generator refuses `override` (row 650). Gated by `compiler_tests/Override*`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-checker-overloading/REPORT.md` section 1.
- F-89 **The one library's ranges of rank 2 and 3 have bounded kinds, their comparisons are declared at the `ZZ32` kinds, and `#(0,n)` is empty.** `BoundedRange2D` and `BoundedRange3D` are the meets of `Range2D` or `Range3D` and `BoundedRange`, and the left, right and full kinds extend them. The generic range traits declare `CMP`, `FORWARD_CMP` and the compact kinds' size abstract, and the `ZZ32` kinds of rank 1 to 3 define them. `#0`, `#(0,n)` and `#(0,n,m)` are empty: `|#(0,3)|` is 0. Gated by `tests/RangeKindBodies.fss`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-range-types/REPORT.md` section 1.
- F-90 **In the interpreter's library, several array and matrix declarations and `SUFFIX_SUM` are written so that the compiled checker accepts them: `__DefaultVector`, `__DefaultMatrix` and `TransposedMatrix` declare the array family's bound `T extends { Number, MultiplicativeRing[\T\] }`, which F-151 owns; `__immutableFactory1` is declared to answer an `ImmutableArray1` (its branch for lowest index 0 is cast to that type, F-264); `__ImmutableSubArray1` has no `put`; `Matrix`'s `mul` writes its two parallel calls, once a tuple typed `((), ())`, as a parallel `do … also do … end` block, typed `()`; and `TransposedMatrix`'s `add`, `subtract` and `negate` call `Matrix`'s operators.** The unary operator `SUFFIX_SUM` on a `ZZ32` array (`FortressLibrary.fsi`) loops over `seq((0 # (|x| - 1)).reverse)`, since a strided range `a:b:c` is declared `Range[\ZZ32\]`, which is no generator, so the checker refuses `seq(a:b:c)` (row 661, open). The same change made `String`'s `left` and `right` answer `Just(c)` (P-53, built), and `QQ`'s `ceiling` and `truncate` raise `DivisionByZero` at +∞, −∞ and 0/0, P-54's present rule; P-54's later change, after the switch-over, is still to build. The distance stage shows that the checker accepts these declarations: none of its sites is in them (F-53, which lists the five). Under walk, `tests/TransposedMatrixAndFreeze.fss` checks the values of `mul`, of the factory's callers `replica` and `freeze`, of the sub-array and of the transposed arithmetic, and `tests/IntegerOrderNumerals.fss` checks `SUFFIX_SUM`'s; no test covers the bound. `tests/StringPieces.fss` and `tests/NumberOrderListDeclarations.fss` check the `String` and `QQ` parts. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-library-slips/REPORT.md` sections 1 and 6.
- F-91 **The one library's `narrowToRange` and its bounds check are declared at the range kinds over `ZZ32` of rank 1 to 3.** Each kind also declares the meet with an `OpenRange`, which the checker requires. The checks are `checkSelection`, `checkSelection2D` and `checkSelection3D`, named by rank since walk refuses overloads of one name over two instantiations of `Range` (row 416). At rank 2 and 3 the check, and so the arrays' range subscripts, build P-52. `(:)`'s five cutting methods fail (P-56). Gated by `tests/RangeNarrowKinds.fss`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-range-kinds/REPORT.md` section 1.
- F-92 **The one library's order operators on pairs and triples bound each element by `StandardPartialOrder`, so walk refuses at the call a tuple with an element of another type.** It refuses it also where earlier elements decide, as `(1,()) < (2,())`, and for numbers of two run-time types at one position, whose join it takes (row 511), as `(1,2) < (1,2.5)`. Operands declared with one type convert and compare. Unordered deciding elements give `false`, or `Unordered` for `CMP`. Gated by `tests/TupleOrder*`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-tuple-orders/REPORT.md` sections 1 and 6.
- F-93 **A generator's size is a counted default on `Generator`, the relational predicate reads neither a size nor an index, and `Indexed`'s default index-value pairs keep the indexed value's indices.** A type with its own `|self|` keeps it. Two answers differ from the team's library: `increasing((0#4).reverse)` fails where it held, and the default pairs of a value indexed from 5 are indexed from 5, not 0. - F-122 **`round` on an `RR64` or an `RR32` sends an exact half to the even integer on both paths.** NaN gives 0, and a value beyond the `ZZ64` range saturates to the `ZZ64` bounds. On both paths, a numeral within half an ulp of a tie is rounded as its nearest double, not as the rational that it denotes, against the specification (row 360). The ties are gated under walk by `tests/RoundHalfEvenRungR.fss`, and on the compiled path, for `RR64`, by `library_tests/RR64FunctionsRungF.fss`; the compiled `RR32` ties were observed in a probe of the report. NaN and saturation are gated on neither path: they were observed in the report's walk probe and compiled differential, and read in the code (`(long) Math.rint` in `Float.java:384`, `RR32.java:326` and `simpleDoubleArith.java:132-134`). Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-round-half-even/REPORT.md`, "What landed" and "Differentials".
- F-123 **A compiled object with no `asString` of its own prints its bare type name, as walk does.** A value whose run-time Java class declares its own `toString`, such as the compiled `RR32`'s, prints by it. Open on the compiled path: an object that declares or inherits a zero-argument Fortress member named `toString` overflows the stack when it is printed (row 321), and `asDebugString` and `asExprString` print differently from walk's, where the specification is silent (row 363). For a string static argument walk is the one that is wrong: it takes the argument from the run-time class, so `Cell("s")` prints `Cell[\FlatString\]`, where the compiled `Cell[\String\]` is the specification's answer (row 364). For a numeral argument neither path gives the specification's type. Gated by `compiler_tests/DefaultRenderRungS`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-default-rendering/REPORT.md`, "Defects and their homes".
- F-124 **On the compiled path, at or beyond the width of `ZZ32` or `ZZ64`, `LSHIFT` gives 0 and `RSHIFT` the sign; both reverse on a negative count, and `narrow` keeps the low 32 bits.** "The sign" is 0 for a nonnegative value and -1 for a negative one. `ZZ64`'s and `NN64`'s `narrow` to 32 bits keeps the low 32 bits. `<<`, `>>` and `<<<` keep their own rules, and `asZZ32` throws out of range. Negation, absolute value and division overflow only at the minimum value and test exactly for it, so the minimum raises `IntegerOverflow`, and `|0|`, `-0` and `0 DIV -1` answer 0. Addition and subtraction test the sign bits, and multiplication computes the exact product (`Math.multiplyExact` on `ZZ64`, a range-checked 64-bit product on `ZZ32`). So these raise `IntegerOverflow` on every overflow, and a zero factor answers 0. `ZZ`'s `<<<` raises a catchable `IntegerOverflow` on a shift that it cannot represent (row 386). Gated by `compiler_tests/IntSemanticsRungB.fss`, and for addition and subtraction by the team's `library_tests/Integer3.fss`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-int-semantics-compiled/REPORT.md` section 1.
- F-125 **Under `walk`, `LSHIFT` and `RSHIFT` on the four fixed widths give 0 or the sign at or beyond the width and reverse on a negative count, and `ZZ`'s `shift` is exact.** It builds P-69. `GCD` and `LCM` are nonnegative, and `0 LCM 0` is 0 (row 385). So the team's test `RangePrototype.fss` computes its signed stride with `GCD`. `CHOOSE` answers 0 for `k < 0` or `k > n`. Overflow raises (F-132). The compiler prelude has no `shift` (row 383). Gated by `tests/IntSemanticsRungI.fss`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-int-semantics-walk/REPORT.md` sections 4 and 7.
- F-126 **`ZZ`'s functional method `shift` reserves the name `shift` in every program under walk, and not on the compiled path, whose prelude declares no `shift`.** The `fortress-repo` skill gives the general rule (`references/library.md`). So the library's parameters that `shift` would shadow are named `amount`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-int-semantics-walk/JUDGE.md` section 3; the renames, its `REPORT.md` section 5.
- F-128 **Under `walk`, the interpreter converts by coercion at its three kinds of type check.** They are a parameter, a varargs parameter included; an overloaded call that no declaration fits without coercion, which walk then dispatches again; and a typed binding or assignment. Walk chooses the coercion by the run-time value (P-59). Not converted, as measured: a declared return (row 387), a coercion with its own static parameter (row 513), and an overloaded function's tuple parameter or a tuple-typed field (row 395). Not converted, by the code, and not measured: a varargs or keyword element of the specification's tuple coercion, and its arrow coercion. Gated by `tests/Coercion*RungC.fss`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-interp-coercion/REPORT.md` sections 1, 5 and 9.
- F-129 **A size is carried at run time as a descriptor from `RTTIsize.of`, and a program whose sizes are known at compile time loads, dispatches and runs compiled, apart from the open cases below.** It builds P-41. Each size value, such as the 3 of `Vec[\3\]`, has one descriptor; in a run-time subtype test, it is a supertype only of an equal size. A size read as a value is a constant that the class loader replaces by the numeral. Closures and tasks capture a size as a free static parameter (F-135). A size made from a number known only at run time does not run compiled: `tests/NatReflectTest.fss` stops at load (row 307). Gated by `compiler_tests/NatRt*`. Also open on the compiled path: a `ZZ32Vector` passed to a generic constructor fails at load (row 408); the compiled path gives every static parameter with no `extends` clause, a size among them, the bound `Object`, not the specification's `Any` (row 412); a dispatched overload arm whose static parameter has a concrete generic bound stops the compile in its sized form and dies at load in its type form (row 413); an object that extends two instantiations of one trait, one at a static parameter, passes the checker and dies at load (row 414). Row 416 is walk's defect: walk refuses at load `g(b: Tg[\3\])` beside `g(b: Tg[\4\])`, which the compiled run dispatches, since walk's overloading check applies no exclusion of instantiations. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-size-runtime/REPORT.md` sections 1 and 9.
- F-130 **The specification's wrapping operators ∔, ∸ and ⨰ are declared in the interpreter's library, and the library bodies and team tests that meant to wrap use them.** It builds P-73. The compiler prelude's ∔ and ∸ saturate, and it declares no ⨰ (row 348). One library body uses the operators where wrapping is wrong, by reading, not run (row 700). `Random`'s `LinearCongruential` computes `(mult DOTTIMES widen(state)) DOTPLUS add` and only then takes `MOD modulus`. So it agrees with the true state only where no step overflows or where the modulus divides 2^width of its type `N`. The library builds it only with the modulus 2^48, where it is right. Gated by `tests/WrapOperatorsRungD.fss`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-wrap-operators/REPORT.md` section 2; their users, `reviews/wrap-dependent-code.md`.
- F-131 **The one library's number tower is flat.** It builds P-43. `ZZ32`, `ZZ64`, `NN32`, `NN64`, `ZZ`, `QQ`, `RR64`, `RR32` and `IntLiteral` are siblings under `Number`. `IntLiteral` is the type that the library declares for an integer numeral. The compiled checker gives a numeral that type; walk still gives it `ZZ32`, or `ZZ64` or `ZZ` when its value does not fit (P-76). Each wider integer type converts from each narrower one, and `RR64` from a `ZZ32` and an `IntLiteral`; a `ZZ64` goes into `RR64` only when written out (P-74). `QQ` converts from the five integer types and `IntLiteral`, and `RR64` converts from `RR32` too (F-139). `NN32` does not yet convert into `RR64`: P-75 decides that it will. `Number`'s `=` compares a float with an exact number after `asFloat`, so it is not transitive (row 434). Under walk, a big operator over a list of numerals, with no static argument on either, such as `SUM <|1, 2, 3|>`, finds no matching overload at run time (row 432), and an empty `SUM` over an additive group that is not a number dies (row 436). Gated by `tests/FlatTowerRungF.fss` for every type but `RR32` and `IntLiteral`: that none is another's subtype, their coercions and `=`. `RR32`'s place is gated with F-139, and `IntLiteral`'s with F-79. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-flat-tower/REPORT.md` sections 5 and 17.
- F-132 **Under `walk`, fixed-width integer arithmetic raises `IntegerOverflow` when the result does not fit, as the specification says.** It builds P-73. Every arithmetic operation on a fixed width whose result can leave its type raises it, `^`, `CHOOSE` and `LCM` included, and a program can catch it. Three kinds of operation raise nothing: the wrapping operators (F-130) and `narrow`, the written conversion of a `ZZ64` to `ZZ32` or an `NN64` to `NN32` (P-72), which keep the low bits; and the shifts `LSHIFT` and `RSHIFT`, which lose the bits shifted out (F-125). ## The library's arrays and algebra

- F-151 **In the interpreter's library, `Vector`, `Matrix` and their factories and operators bound their element type by `T extends { Number, MultiplicativeRing[\T\] }`.** `Number` declares no arithmetic, so the compiled checker accepts the bodies' arithmetic only through `MultiplicativeRing[\T\]`. `Number` stays in the bound because its `comprises` clause lists every type below it, so an element type excludes `String`; the ring alone does not give that. That exclusion makes the four juxtapositions of a vector or a matrix with a scalar `T`, in either order, a valid overloading beside the library's juxtapositions with a `String`. `Number` also declares the `asFloat` that the vector norm calls. The eight number types meet the bound. `Number` itself and the numeral type `IntLiteral` do not, since neither is a ring at its own type. So `Vector[\Number,n\]` is not a well-formed type, and `array1` and `array2` have no branch for `Number`: called at `Number`, they give a plain array at run time, not a vector or a matrix (F-229). The checker accepts a call whose argument's type is built from the caller's own type parameter under the same bound, such as the norm's `squaredNorm(me)` (F-227). The scalar extension, the eight operators between an array and a scalar, has bounds of its own, also with `Number` (F-119). Gated under walk by `tests/ArrayElementAlgebra.fss`. The bound is the default that `reviews/array-fork2-judgement.md` recommended. It landed when the curator said to land it. Detail: that judgement, sections 2.5 (what `Number`'s `comprises` clause gives), 2.9, way 3 (the ring alone, measured) and 4 (the bound and its cost).
- F-152 **`Vector` and `Matrix` are the only array traits with an algebra, `AdditiveGroup`, and their element must be a `Number`.** They inherit `+`, `-`, unary `-` and `zero`, and nothing from another algebraic trait. `Array3` has no algebra (row 292). `×` reaches no array, by design: juxtaposition is the inner product (rows 109, 293). Walk accepts, unchecked, a carrier that extends both `Matrix` and `MultiplicativeRing`, and its `+` then fails (row 371). The specification's `T^n` denotes these traits (row 24), and neither path takes it. Detail: `reviews/array-design-ways.md` section 2.
- F-154 **The library declares its matrix and vector products with shared `nat`s, so under walk a product of the wrong shapes stops the run at dispatch.** A shared `nat` is a size parameter that two parameter types name, as `m` in `DOT` and juxtaposition of `Matrix[\T,n,m\]` by `Matrix[\T,m,p\]`. The matrix-vector and vector-matrix products share theirs in the same way. Each product name is overloaded, so the stop reads "Failed to find any matching overload", with the argument types and their sizes. It is a `ProgramError` that no `catch` takes. A declaration that is not overloaded, such as the APL model's `pick`, fails instead with a unification error that names the size; no library product is such a declaration. Detail: `perf-probes/prelude/natives-shape.md` section 1 (the gaps and walk's half: "What each gap does to it", "Limits, by reading"); `perf-probes/prelude/natives-binding-probe.md` section 1 (the compiled half; its section 2 measures the `import java` form, which P-58 did not take).

1	<!-- The curator's decisions about the project (the language, the library, the tree and its tools, the specification and the plan) as they stand now. One line per entry under its permanent number, `- P-48 **Title.** Text.`, written only with `explorations/coordinator/tools/record.py`. `POSITIONS-history.md` holds each change's provenance and the line as it stood before.
